citation: Ulwelling W, Smith K. The Diagnostic Accuracy of Phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in Blood: A Systematic Review. Clin Biochem Rev. 2018.
key_findings_and_parameters: PEth half-life is 4-10 days; detects consumption over prior 2-4 weeks. Thresholds: <20 ng/mL indicates abstinence/light; 20-200 ng/mL indicates moderate/significant; >200 ng/mL indicates heavy/chronic drinking.
limitations_and_assumptions: Measures exposure only, not organ damage; does not distinguish alcoholic cardiomyopathy from other DCM causes; does not predict alcohol withdrawal syndrome severity.

citation: Stewart SH et al. Phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in blood as a marker of unhealthy alcohol use. Addiction. 2014.
key_findings_and_parameters: Sensitivity 88%, specificity 89% for detecting unhealthy drinking (>4 drinks/day or >14 drinks/week).
limitations_and_assumptions: Inter-individual metabolic variation in phospholipid formation; false positives rare but trace detection possible.

citation: Fauchier L et al. Comparison of long-term outcome of alcoholic and idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy. Eur J Heart Fail. 2000.
key_findings_and_parameters: Patients with ACM who achieved complete abstinence had significant LVEF improvement (+13 ± 8% points at 6-12 months). Persistent drinkers had stable or deteriorating LVEF (-2 ± 7% points).
limitations_and_assumptions: Single center; self-reported abstinence in original study (modern studies use PEth); selection bias for survivors.

citation: Nicolas JM et al. The effect of continued drinking on the outcome of alcoholic cardiomyopathy. Ann Intern Med. 2002.
key_findings_and_parameters: Patients with baseline LVEF <35% showed marked LVEF increase (mean +14.2% points) upon abstinence or reduction to <20 g/day. Non-abstainers showed 0.5% change and higher mortality.
limitations_and_assumptions: Conducted in male cohort; generalizability to female patients required subsequent modeling.

citation: Fernandez-Sola J et al. Comparison of alcoholic cardiomyopathy in men and women. Alcohol Clin Exp Res. 2006.
key_findings_and_parameters: Women develop ACM at lower cumulative lifetime alcohol doses (60% of male dose) but demonstrate comparable reverse remodeling potential upon abstinence.
limitations_and_assumptions: Smaller sample size of female cohort; simulated cohort must reflect real-world 3:1 to 4:1 male-to-female ratio.

citation: Herman DS et al. Truncations of Titin Causing Dilated Cardiomyopathy. N Engl J Med. 2012.
key_findings_and_parameters: TTN truncating variants (TTNtv) present in 25% of familial DCM and 18% of sporadic DCM, predominantly in A-band. Missense variants have high benign frequency and are classified as VUS.
limitations_and_assumptions: VUS must never be treated as pathogenic; TTNtv status does not guarantee non-recovery but may alter remodeling dynamics.

citation: Ware JS et al. Genetic Architecture of Dilated Cardiomyopathy. N Engl J Med. 2016.
key_findings_and_parameters: Identified excess TTNtv burden in patients with secondary/toxin-associated DCM (including alcohol), supporting a two-hit hypothesis where alcohol triggers severe dysfunction in genetically susceptible hosts.
limitations_and_assumptions: Two-hit hypothesis supported biologically but exact individual interaction odds requires simulation modeling.

topic: Cardiac MRI LGE Fibrosis in DCM
citation: Gulati A et al. Association of mid-wall fibrosis with mortality and sudden death in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy. JAMA. 2013.
key_findings_and_parameters: Mid-wall LGE replacement fibrosis present in 30% of non-ischemic DCM. Absence of LGE is strongly associated with functional recovery, whereas extensive LGE (>5% LV mass) portends permanent scar.
limitations_and_assumptions: LGE measures focal replacement scar; diffuse interstitial fibrosis requires T1 mapping/ECV which is not uniformly available.

citation: Halliday BP et al. Association Between Midwall Late Gadolinium Enhancement and Sudden Cardiac Death in Patients With Dilated Cardiomyopathy. Circulation. 2017.
key_findings_and_parameters: Patients without LGE showed significantly greater reverse remodeling (+11.8% LVEF recovery) compared to patients with extensive midwall LGE (+3.2% LVEF recovery).
limitations_and_assumptions: Observational CMR data; LGE does not preclude medical optimization.

citation: Bernard O et al. Deep Learning Techniques for Automatic MRI Segmentation: The ACDC Challenge. IEEE TMI. 2018.
key_findings_and_parameters: Establishes reference distributions for short-axis CMR: DCM mean LVEDV 235 ± 68 mL, mean LVEF 34 ± 11%, myocardial mass 142 ± 38 g.
limitations_and_assumptions: ACDC cohort does not include alcohol exposure or genetic data; structural distributions serve as physical baseline only.
